\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Codec --- Langs: Results}

\begin{definition}[Valid configuration encoding language]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.validLang}
\label{Complexity.Codec.validLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols. The
valid-configuration language consists of Boolean strings $y$ for which there exist a
Boolean string $x$ and natural numbers $c,s$ such that $y$ is the pair encoding of $x$
and the pair encoding of the binary representations of $c$ and $s$, and there is a
configuration $C$ of $N$ on input $x$ that lies in the window of size $s$ and has
configuration code $c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial configuration encoding language]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.initLang}
\label{Complexity.Codec.initLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols. The
initial-configuration encoding language consists of Boolean strings $y$ for which there
exist a Boolean string $x$ and natural numbers $c,s$ such that $y$ is the pair encoding
of $x$ and the pair encoding of the binary representations of $c$ and $s$, and the
initial configuration of $N$ on input $x$ has configuration code $c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Accepting configuration encoding language]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.acceptLang}
\label{Complexity.Codec.acceptLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols. The
accepting-configuration encoding language consists of Boolean strings $y$ for which
there exist a Boolean string $x$ and natural numbers $c,s$ such that $y$ is the pair
encoding of $x$ and the pair encoding of the binary representations of $c$ and $s$, and
there is a configuration $C$ of $N$ on input $x$ that lies in the window of size $s$,
has configuration code $c$, has no current state, and has output consisting of the
single Boolean value true.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One-step configuration encoding language]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.stepLang}
\label{Complexity.Codec.stepLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.NDTM.CfgStep, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols. The
one-step configuration language consists of Boolean strings $y$ for which there exist a
Boolean string $x$ and natural numbers $c,c',s$ such that $y$ is the nested pair
encoding of $x$ and the binary representations of $c,c',s$, and there are configurations
$C,C'$ of $N$ on input $x$ such that $C$ lies in the window of size $s$ and has code
$c$, $C'$ follows $C$ in one machine step, $C'$ also lies in that window, and $C'$ has
code $c'$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Injectivity of pair encoding]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.pairEncode_inj}
\label{Complexity.Codec.pairEncode_inj}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode_injective}
\difficulty{3}
If two pair encodings of bit strings are equal, then their first components are equal
and their second components are equal.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in the valid-configuration language]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.mem_validLang}
\label{Complexity.Codec.mem_validLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.pairEncode_inj, Complexity.Codec.validLang, Complexity.LogProg.bits_injective, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input, let $x$ be a
Boolean string, and let $c,s$ be natural numbers. The paired encoding of $x$ with the
paired encodings of the binary expansions of $c$ and $s$ belongs to the
valid-configuration language of $N$ if and only if there is a configuration $C$ on input
$x$ whose work-tape heads and nonblank cells lie within distance $s$ of the origin and
whose configuration code at window size $s$ is $c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in the initial-configuration language]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.mem_initLang}
\label{Complexity.Codec.mem_initLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.initLang, Complexity.Codec.pairEncode_inj, Complexity.LogProg.bits_injective, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input, let $x$ be a
Boolean string, and let $c,s$ be natural numbers. The paired encoding of $x$ with the
paired encodings of the binary expansions of $c$ and $s$ belongs to the
initial-configuration language of $N$ if and only if the code, at window size $s$, of
$N$'s initial configuration on input $x$ equals $c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in the acceptance language]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.mem_acceptLang}
\label{Complexity.Codec.mem_acceptLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.pairEncode_inj, Complexity.LogProg.bits_injective, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input, and let $x$ be a
Boolean string and $c,s$ be natural numbers. The paired encoding of $x$ with the paired
encodings of the binary expansions of $c$ and $s$ belongs to the acceptance language of
$N$ if and only if there is a configuration $C$ of $N$ on input $x$ whose work-tape
heads and nonblank cells lie within distance $s$ of the origin, whose configuration code
at window size $s$ is $c$, whose state is halted, and whose output is exactly the
one-bit string $[1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in the one-step language]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.mem_stepLang}
\label{Complexity.Codec.mem_stepLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.pairEncode_inj, Complexity.Codec.stepLang, Complexity.LogProg.bits_injective, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.NDTM.CfgStep, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input, let $x$ be a
Boolean string, and let $c,c',s$ be natural numbers. The paired encoding of $x$, $c$,
$c'$, and $s$ belongs to the one-step language of $N$ if and only if there are
configurations $C,C'$ on input $x$ such that $C$ lies within window $s$ and has code
$c$, $C'$ is obtained from $C$ by one step of $N$ and lies within window $s$, and $C'$
has code $c'$.
\end{theorem}
